subject: chemistry
title: Changes Between States
welcome_lead: Heat up, cool down: watch matter transform from one state to another.
meta_desc: Learn melting, freezing, boiling, condensing and sublimation in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You can now name every change of state in the universe.

concepts.def: Solid changing to liquid when heated.
Liquid changing to solid when cooled.
Liquid changing to gas throughout, at boiling point.
Gas changing to liquid when cooled.
Liquid turning to gas from the surface only.
Solid changing straight to a gas, skipping liquid.

walkthroughs.body_html: When you heat a solid, its particles vibrate faster. At the melting point the solid melts into a liquid. Heat the liquid more and at the boiling point it boils into a gas.

Cooling reverses everything. A gas condenses into a liquid, and a liquid freezes into a solid.

For pure water: freezing point = 0°C, boiling point = 100°C.

Some substances skip the liquid stage. Sublimation is when a solid turns straight into a gas. Solid carbon dioxide (dry ice) does this at room temperature.

Iodine and dry ice sublime!

mcqs.q: What is the change from gas to liquid called?
options: Condensing
Melting
Subliming
Freezing

mcqs.q: Which process turns a solid directly into a gas?
options: Boiling
Sublimation
Evaporation
Melting

mcqs.q: Why does the colour of a transition metal complex change when ligands are exchanged?
options: Different ligands cause different amounts of d-orbital splitting, so different wavelengths of light are absorbed.
The colour changes because the metal ion itself changes oxidation state.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.

mcqs.q: What is the product of mild oxidation of a primary alcohol?
options: An aldehyde (which can be further oxidised to a carboxylic acid).
A primary alcohol is oxidised directly to a ketone.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
A primary alcohol is oxidised to an alkene by losing water.
